'''Kentavious Tannell Caldwell-Pope''' ({{IPAc-en|k|ɛ|n|'|t|eɪ|v|i|ə|s}} {{respell|ken|TAY|vee|əs}};<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 17, 2024}}</ref> {{ne}} '''Caldwell'''; born February 18, 1993), also known by his initials '''KCP''', is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was named a [[McDonald's All-American]] as one of the top high school basketball players in the class of 2011. He played [[college basketball]] for two years with the [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia Bulldogs]] in the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC), and was voted the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] as a sophomore in 2013.

Caldwell-Pope was selected with the eighth overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He played four seasons with the Pistons before joining the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] as a free agent in 2017–18. He won his first NBA championship with the Lakers in [[2020 NBA Finals|2020]]. He spent a season with the [[Washington Wizards]] after having been traded there from the Lakers in August 2021, and was subsequently traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in July 2022, winning his second NBA championship in [[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]. He has also played for the [[Orlando Magic]].

==Early life==
Caldwell-Pope was born as Kentavious Caldwell to Rhonda Caldwell and Lawrence Pope.<ref name="hummer">{{cite web |last1=Hummer |first1=Steve |date=February 3, 2013 |title=Sadly for Bulldogs, there’s only one Caldwell-Pope |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/sadly-for-bulldogs-there-only-one-caldwell-pope/0BNFHK662l9ji4XxsJuYsI/ |access-date=June 4, 2025 |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution}}</ref> He decided to add his father's surname to his own when he was a junior in high school.<ref name="hummer" />

==High school career==
Caldwell-Pope was a highly heralded player in high school. As a senior, he averaged 31 points and 8.2 rebounds per game at [[Greenville High School (Greenville, Georgia)|Greenville High School]] in [[Greenville, Georgia]]. He led the Patriots to the State Class A Final Four in 2011 and to consecutive Sweet 16 berths in 2009–10.

He was named to several prominent high school All-America teams as a senior, including being selected to play in the [[2011 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2011 McDonald's All-American Game]]<ref name="MCD">{{Cite web |last=White |first=Chris |date=February 10, 2011 |title=High school basketball: Greenville's Caldwell-Pope named a McDonald's All-American |url=http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/2011/02/10/1454929/high-school-basksetball-greenvilles.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306111449/http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/2011/02/10/1454929/high-school-basksetball-greenvilles.html |archive-date=March 6, 2014 |access-date=March 16, 2013 |publisher=Ledger-Enquirer}}</ref> and the [[Jordan Brand Classic]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150207194131/http://jordanbrandclassic.com/Teams/2011-jordan-brand-classic-west-team.html 2011 Jordan Brand Classic: West Team], jordanbrandclassic.com. Retrieved March 15, 2011.</ref>

As a senior, he was rated the nation's No. 3 shooting guard prospect, the No. 12 prospect overall, by recruiting analysts for [[Rivals.com]].

Caldwell-Pope chose Georgia to play for Mark Fox and Cody Anderson over scholarship offers from Alabama, Florida State, Georgia Tech, and Tennessee, among others.

==College career==
[[file:Kentavious Caldwell-Pope 2012.jpg|thumb|150px|Caldwell-Pope playing for Georgia in 2012]]
As a freshman at Georgia, Caldwell-Pope was named to the Coaches' Freshman All-SEC Team, which also included NBA lottery picks [[Bradley Beal]], [[Anthony Davis]], and [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist]]. His highest output as a freshman was 25 points against Ole Miss, which was the most by a UGA freshman in almost 13 years.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 21, 2012 |title=Mississippi 66, Georgia 63 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=320210061 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116080744/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=320210061 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 16, 2017 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

As a sophomore, Caldwell-Pope was named [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] after averaging 18.5 points and 7.1 rebounds per game.<ref name="POY">{{Cite web |last=Lockridge & Cole |date=March 12, 2013 |title=Georgia's Kentavious Caldwell-Pope named SEC's top player |url=http://www.tennessean.com/article/20130312/SPORTS06/303120093/Georgia-s-Kentavious-Caldwell-Pope-named-SEC-s-top-player |access-date=March 16, 2013 |publisher=The Tennessean}}</ref> In his final collegiate game, he scored a career-high 32 points and 13 rebounds in a loss against [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] at the [[2013 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] in Nashville.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 14, 2013 |title=LSU 68, Georgia 63 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330730061 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> He [[NBA draft declaration|declared for the NBA draft]] after the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 15, 2013 |title=Georgia sophomore star entering NBA draft |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/sec/2013/04/15/georgia-sophomore-star-entering-nba-draft/2084371/ |access-date=April 15, 2013 |publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Detroit Pistons (2013–2017)===
On June 27, 2013, Caldwell-Pope was selected with the eighth overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He later joined the Pistons for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]] and signed his rookie scale contract with the team on July 19.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 19, 2013 |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Draft Selections Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Tony Mitchell |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-draft-selections-kentavious-caldwell-pope-and-tony-mitchell |access-date=July 19, 2013 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> On April 16, 2014, he scored a then-career-high 30 points in a loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 16, 2014 |title=Notebook: Thunder 112, Pistons 111 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140416/DETOKC/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140429203839/http://www.nba.com/games/20140416/DETOKC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=April 29, 2014 |access-date=April 16, 2014 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref>

In July 2014, Caldwell-Pope rejoined the Pistons for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 24 points and 7.4 rebounds in five games. Head coach [[Stan Van Gundy]] quickly assessed Caldwell-Pope as his best perimeter defender and he wound up leading the Pistons in minutes played with 2,587. Caldwell-Pope got better after the All-Star break, largely thanks to the acquisition of point guard [[Reggie Jackson (basketball, born 1990)|Reggie Jackson]]; post All-Star Break, Caldwell-Pope averaged 14.3 points per game. He finished the season with 153 three-point shots made, 70 more than the closest Pistons player. He tied [[Kevin Love]] for 16th in the NBA.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 4, 2015 |title=2014-15 Player Recap: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/features/2014-15-player-recap-kentavious-caldwell-pope |access-date=November 3, 2015 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref>
[[File:Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (30851390714).jpg|thumb|left|Caldwell-Pope with the Pistons in December 2016, shooting over [[Marcin Gortat]] of the Washington Wizards]]
On December 16, 2015, Caldwell-Pope scored a then career-high 31 points in a 119–116 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 16, 2015 |title=Caldwell-Pope scores 31 points, Pistons beat Celtics 119-116 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151216/BOSDET/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622004936/http://www.nba.com/games/20151216/BOSDET/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 22, 2017 |access-date=December 16, 2015 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> He helped the Pistons finish the 2015–16 regular season with a 44–38 record, which was good for the eighth seed in the Eastern Conference. The Pistons thus qualified for the playoffs for the first time since 2009. In the first round of the playoffs, the Pistons faced the first-seeded [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], and in a Game 1 loss on April 17, Caldwell-Pope scored a team-high 21 points.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 17, 2016 |title=Big 3 back together, lead Cavs to 106-101 win over Pistons |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160417/DETCLE/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417205636/http://www.nba.com/games/20160417/DETCLE/gameinfo.html |archive-date=April 17, 2016 |access-date=April 18, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Pistons went on to lose the series 4–0.

On November 9, 2016, Caldwell-Pope scored a then season-high 27 points in a 107–100 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 9, 2016 |title=Bledsoe, Dudley lead Suns past Pistons 105-99 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899563 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On November 25, 2016, he recorded 16 points and a career-high 10 assists in a 108–97 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 25, 2016 |title=Pistons hand Clippers first road loss with 108-97 win |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899680 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On January 8, 2017, he hit a three-pointer with 9.4 seconds left in double overtime to lead the Pistons to a 125–124 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]; he finished with 26 points.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 8, 2017 |title=Pistons outlast Trail Blazers 125-124 in double-overtime |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400933467 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On February 1, 2017, he scored a career-high 38 points in a 118–98 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. He also made a career-high eight three-pointers on 11 attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 1, 2017 |title=Caldwell-Pope scores 38 in Pistons' 118-98 win over Pelicans |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899400 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On February 23, 2017, Caldwell-Pope scored 33 points, including three three-pointers late in the fourth quarter during a Detroit rally, as the Pistons defeated the [[Charlotte Hornets]] 114–108 in overtime. Caldwell-Pope's three-pointer with 18.2 seconds to play tied the game at 100.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 23, 2017 |title=Pistons rally from 18 down, beat Hornets 114-108 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900257 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On June 23, 2017, Caldwell-Pope was suspended for two games without pay by the NBA for pleading guilty to operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 23, 2017 |title=Detroit Pistons guard Kentavious Caldwell-Pope suspended for 2 games |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2017/06/23/pistons-guard-kentavious-caldwell-pope-suspended-2-games |access-date=June 23, 2017 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On July 7, 2017, the Pistons renounced the rights to Caldwell-Pope, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Langlois |first=Keith |date=July 7, 2017 |title=Detroit Pistons Renounce Rights to Kentavious Caldwell-Pope |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-renounce-rights-kentavious-caldwell-pope |access-date=July 7, 2017 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2017–2021)===
On July 13, 2017, Caldwell-Pope signed a one-year, $18 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 13, 2017 |title=Lakers Sign Kentavious Caldwell-Pope |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170713-caldwell-pope-signed |access-date=July 13, 2017 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Beacham |first1=Greg |last2=Krawczynski |first2=Jon |date=July 12, 2017 |title=Reports: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Los Angeles Lakers reach 1-year deal |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2017/07/12/report-kentavious-caldwell-pope-los-angeles-lakers-reach-1-year-deal |access-date=July 22, 2017 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He made his debut for the Lakers on October 22, 2017, scoring 20 points as a starter in a 119–112 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 22, 2017 |title=Wiggins' heave banks in, leads Timberwolves past Thunder |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974790 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On November 27, 2017, he scored a season-high 29 points against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kentavious Caldwell-Pope 2017-18 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/caldwke01/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> On December 13, 2017, Caldwell-Pope pleaded guilty to a probation violation he committed during the summer. He was handed a 25-day jail sentence, but under a [[work-release program]], was allowed to leave the facility for home games and practices. He was not allowed to leave California, limiting him to only home games within the state during that period.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ganguli |first=Tania |date=December 21, 2017 |title=Kentavious Caldwell-Pope is practicing and playing with the Lakers while serving a 25-day jail sentence |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-caldwell-pope-20171221-story.html |access-date=December 23, 2017 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> On February 24, 2018, he scored a season-high 34 points and hit a career-high-tying eight 3-pointers in a 113–108 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2018 |title=Caldwell-Pope's season-high 34 points help Lakers top Kings |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975637 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On March 22, 2018, he hit eight 3-pointers and had 28 points in a 128–125 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 22, 2018 |title=Davis, Rondo, push Pelicans past Lakers, 128-125 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975821 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On July 6, 2018, Caldwell-Pope re-signed with the Lakers,<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2018 |title=Lakers Re-Sign Kentavious Caldwell-Pope |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180706-lakers-re-sign-kentavious-caldwell-pope?ls=recent_news |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> on a reported one-year, $12 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barnewall |first=Chris |date=July 2, 2018 |title=2018 NBA free agency: Lakers, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope agree to deal after LeBron's commitment |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2018-nba-free-agency-lakers-kentavious-caldwell-pope-agree-to-deal-after-lebrons-commitment/ |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> On December 16, 2018, he scored a season-high 25 points in a 128–110 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 16, 2018 |title=Wall's 40, 14 lead Wiz past Lakers 128-110; LBJ scores 13 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071120 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On December 30, he set a new season high with 26 points in a 121–114 win over the Kings.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2018 |title=Lakers rally in 4th quarter, defeat Kings 121-112 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071217 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On March 19, he had a season-high 35 points in a 115–101 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 19, 2019 |title=Bucks beat Lakers 115-101; Antetokounmpo, James sit out |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071734 |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In 2019, Caldwell-Pope re-signed with the Lakers once again, this time on a two-year contract worth roughly $16 million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2019 |title=Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Lakers Agree to Reported 2-Year Contract Worth $16M |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2811184-report-kentavious-caldwell-pope-lakers-agree-to-2-year-16m-contract |access-date=July 6, 2019 |website=BleacherReport.com}}</ref> In [[2019–20 Los Angeles Lakers season|2019–20]], he made a career-high 38.5% of his 3-pointers and was third on the team with 92 made 3-pointers.<ref name="mcmenamin_11222020">{{Cite news |last=McMenamin |first=Dave |date=November 22, 2020 |title=Kentavious Caldwell-Pope nets a three-year, $40 million deal to return to Los Angeles Lakers, agent says |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30361700/kentavious-caldwell-pope-nets-3-year-40-million-deal-return-los-angeles-lakers-report-says |access-date=November 23, 2020}}</ref> Caldwell-Pope won his first NBA championship when the Lakers defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in six games in the [[2020 NBA Finals]]. He was instrumental in the victory, especially in game 4 when his five straight points late in the fourth quarter helped the Lakers pull away from the Heat and sealed the win in that game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Elliott |first=Helene |date=October 7, 2020 |title=Kentavious Caldwell-Pope again proves his worth to the Lakers in Game 4 against the Heat |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2020-10-07/kentavious-caldwell-pope-proves-his-worth-to-the-lakers-in-game-4-against-the-heat# |access-date=October 7, 2020 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> He started all 21 games in the playoffs, averaging 10.7 points in 29 minutes per game and making 37.8% of his 3-pointers.<ref name=mcmenamin_11222020/><ref name="lakers_11222020">{{Cite web |date=November 22, 2020 |title=Lakers Re-sign Kentavious Caldwell-Pope |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-resign-kentavious-caldwell-pope-free-agency2021 |access-date=November 23, 2020 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

Caldwell-Pope declined his player option on the second year of his contract and became a free agent.<ref name=mcmenamin_11222020/> On November 23, 2020, he re-signed with the Lakers on a three-year, $40 million deal.<ref name=mcmenamin_11222020/><ref name=lakers_11222020/>

===Washington Wizards (2021–2022)===
[[File:NBA 2021 - Wizards vs. Hawks, Oct 29 2021 47 (51637106253) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Caldwell-Pope of the [[Washington Wizards]] drives past [[Trae Young]] of the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in 2021]]
On August 6, 2021, Caldwell-Pope was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] as part of a package for [[Russell Westbrook]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/washington-acquires-six-players-five-team-trade|title=Washington acquires six players in five-team trade|work=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021}}</ref> In 77 games with the team, he averaged 13.2 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 1.9 assists per game.

===Denver Nuggets (2022–2024)===
On July 6, 2022, Caldwell-Pope was traded, alongside [[Ish Smith]], to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Monté Morris]] and [[Will Barton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-kentavious-caldwell-pope-and-ish-smith|title=Nuggets Acquire Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Ish Smith|work=nba.com|date=July 6, 2022|access-date=July 6, 2022}}</ref> On July 16, Caldwell-Pope signed a two-year, $30 million contract extension with the Nuggets.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 17, 2022 |title=Nuggets Sign Caldwell-Pope to Contract Extension |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-caldwell-pope-to-contract-extension |access-date=July 18, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Singer |first=Mike |date=July 13, 2022 |title=Kentavious Caldwell-Pope signs two-year $30 million extension with Nuggets |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2022/07/13/kentavious-caldwell-pope-signs-two-year-30-million-extension-nuggets/ |access-date=July 18, 2022 |website=[[The Denver Post]]}}</ref> He made his Nuggets debut on October 19, recording two points, four rebounds, six assists and two steals in a 123–102 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NEW-LOOK JAZZ BEAT NUGGETS 123-102 IN SEASON OPENER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200012 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In Game 5 of the  [[2023 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], Caldwell-Pope put up 11 points, four rebounds, two assists, two steals, three blocks and grabbed the series-clinching rebound before dribbling out the final seconds on the clock in a 94–89 win over the [[Miami Heat]] to help the Nuggets win their first NBA championship in franchise history, awarding Caldwell-Pope his second ring.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nuggets-news-kentavious-caldwell-pope-jimmy-butler-pocket-for-greatest-defensive-play-in-franchise-history|title=Kentavious Caldwell-Pope picks Jimmy Butler's pocket for greatest defensive play in Nuggets franchise history|website=ClutchPoints|last=Villas|first=Rexwell|date=June 12, 2023|access-date=June 12, 2023}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2024–2025)===
On July 6, 2024, Caldwell-Pope signed a three-year, $66 million contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agent Kentavious Caldwell-Pope|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-free-agent-kentavious-caldwell-pope-20240706|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}}</ref> Caldwell-Pope started all 77 games he appeared in during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 8.7 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 1.8 assists.

=== Memphis Grizzlies (2025–2026) ===
On June 15, 2025, Caldwell-Pope was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], alongside [[Cole Anthony]], four unprotected first-round picks including the 16th overall pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]], and a 2029 first-round pick swap in exchange for [[Desmond Bane]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies acquire Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Cole Anthony, four future First Round Picks and one First Round Pick Swap from Magic|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-kentavious-caldwell-pope-cole-anthony-four-future-first-round-picks-and-one-first-round-pick-swap-from-magic|website=NBA.com|date=June 15, 2025|access-date=June 15, 2025}}</ref> He made 51 appearances (including 14 starts) for the Grizzlies during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 8.4 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.7 assists. On February 19, 2026, it was announced that Caldwell-Pope would require season-ending surgery to address "misalignment of his right pinky finger."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies' Kentavious Caldwell-Pope to miss rest of season with finger injury|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2026/02/19/kentavious-caldwell-pope-injury-update-memphis-grizzlies/88768300007/|access-date=February 22, 2026|website=commercialappeal.com|language=en}}</ref> After the season, he reached a buyout agreement with the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite news|title=Caldwell-Pope reaches buyout agreement with Grizzlies|date=July 25, 2026|publisher=The Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/grizzlies-caldwellpope-a54eb9d4ddc4b44ece1cc9d60a04b367|access-date=July 29, 2026}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2026–present)===
On August 5, 2026, Caldwell-Pope signed a one–year, $3.8 million contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Two-Time NBA Champion Kentavious Caldwell-Pope|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-two-time-nba-champion-kentavious-caldwell-pope|access-date=August 27, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref>
